messages.text:
At dawn a battered schooner limps into the channel, her crew waving at the tower.
{#if query told(:storm)}Hesketh weeps openly. You kept your promise.{/if}
In the morning the shore is strewn with timber. The lamp was dark.
You walk inland and do not look back at the tower.
The door is iron-banded and locked.
An hour's sleep would steady you.
Fishwives and chandlers call their wares.
Old Hesketh looks up from his pipe.
"Six measures of oil a night, lad. Less and she goes dark before dawn."
Ask why the lamp room is locked
He fishes in his coat. "My knees can't manage the stair. Take this."
Tell him about the falling glass
His face goes grey. "Then the lamp must burn all that night, whatever it costs."
{#variant 1}He talks about wrecks.{#variant 1}He talks about his late wife.{#variant 1}He says nothing, and that is fine.{/variant}

The lens is taller than you are.
{#if query lit(:lamp)}It burns, throwing its beam across the marsh.{#else}It is cold and dark.{/if}
Strike a match and light it
Pour in the can of oil
{#variant 1}The stallholder eyes your purse.{#variant 1}"Best in Saltmarsh," she says.{/variant}
A sailor muttering about a storm
"Glass is falling. Big blow coming in three days, mark me."
